notes: An escort quest, and almost nothing in it is observable. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a real gate rather than commentary -- only ONE Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet quest can be completed per Vana'dielian day across the whole of Abyssea -- and no packet reports a Vana'dielian day boundary, so it is a note and a flag and the quest is demoted for it. Bullets 3 and 4 are merged into one step: both happen at (G-5) and the marker would not move between guiding the bird there and clicking the supply container, so two rungs at one coordinate would be noise. That container is named twice and differently -- 'the Repair Crate located at (G-5)' in bullet 3, 'the large Repair Trunk' in bullet 4. They may be two objects or one object under two names; the step's action is the click, so the click bullet's name is the one recorded, and both are kept here. Neither is in OBJECT_DENY, so whichever name is right keeps its marker and the wrong one would simply never draw -- a silent loss, not a wrong marker. The Chocobo Blinkers sub-bullet is technique, not a step: they are an aid, they are consumed a minute at a time, and a player who buys none still finishes, so they are not evidence of anything and get no rung. Bullet 7 sits under 'Effects on Bastion:' and is an outcome. Nothing here grants a key item, so every evidence is null and the ladder rests entirely on the session latch. Fame 'amis' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so the region is null and only the raw is kept.

notes: The Samurai unlock, and an unusually well-written page: a two-NM ladder with four observable rungs. 'Level: 30+ any job' is the level gate restated -- level 30 and jobs stays EMPTY; gating the job-unlock quest to a job would lock it away from exactly the people who need it. Bullet 6 carries a purchase, a journey and a trade. The purchase is not a step: 'you must be holding a Hatchet' is what `items` is for, so the Hatchet rides on the trade that consumes it rather than becoming a marker-less rung of its own. Bullet 7 carries two actions -- the Treant has to die between the two ??? interactions -- so it splits, which also makes Zi'Tah mirror Konschtat: trade to spawn, kill, collect. Both ??? are in OBJECT_DENY and can never carry a marker, but they keep their rungs and the last of them carries the Sacred Branch. Bullet 9 never names whom you return to; it can only be Jaucribaix, whom bullets 1 and 8 both name, so recording him is a reading and not an invention. It stays a rung of its own rather than merging into bullet 8 because readiness differs: bullet 8 wants both crafted parts in hand, bullet 9 wants nothing but 72 in-game hours, which no packet reports. The Mumeito is a reward and so can never be evidence; the whole 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is one bullet telling you to keep it for The Sacred Katana or pay Ranemaud 30,000 gil, which is advice, not a step. Fame 'Outlands' is not one of the nine regions, so the region is null. VERIFY: step 10 demoted to medium -- bullet 9 names no target at all, so Jaucribaix there is a reading carried in from bullets 1 and 8; the note conceded that while the confidence denied it. Everything else on this quest survived the adversary pass unchanged.

notes: Three steps and no ambiguity anywhere -- the Rune Fencer unlock. Bullet 4 is the outcome, not a step: job access and a Sowilo Claymore, and the claymore is in the Reward list so it could never be evidence anyway. The Yahse wildflower petal is the only observable thing in the quest and it is granted at bullet 2, so that is the only place it can sit. Bullet 3's long sub-bullet block is Octavien's escalating insults on every tenth failure; it is pure flavour, and the only load-bearing sentence in it is that the attempt takes between 1 and 100 tries and apparently cannot truly fail -- which makes step 3 a loop the ladder cannot count through, since nothing distinguishes attempt 1 from attempt 99. 'Level: 30+' names no job, so it is the level gate only and jobs stays empty; gating the Rune Fencer unlock to RUN would lock it away from everyone who needs it. Adoulin is not one of the nine fame regions, so the region is null and only the raw is kept. The Next field lists two follow-ons and is not a gate on this quest.

notes:
A logic puzzle wearing a fetch quest. The unnumbered notice at the top is a precondition and not a step -- one game day AND a re-zone after What Price Loyalty before this will start, neither of which is observable, which is what demotes the quest. Bullet 1 is deliberately NOT a step: an Elixir is a common consumable that plenty of players already carry, so making 'you hold an Elixir' a rung would jump the ladder for anyone who happens to have one; `items` on the trade step asserts the same requirement without that risk, and bullet 1 is cited there so it stays auditable. Bullet 4 is description -- its three sub-bullets name and place the imps -- and bullet 5 is the action, so bullet 4's names land on bullet 5's steps. The three imps are an unordered group and all draw at once: the page says outright that one or two may be enough and that you do not need to speak to all three, so a strict ladder would mark Rikke and nothing else. Bullet 6 cannot name its target and no reading fixes that -- which imp is honest is redrawn every game day, and the page's table is a deduction key over three scenarios rather than an answer. Naming one would be a wrong marker a third of the time, so that step keeps its zone and loses its marker, with all three candidates in the note. Nothing in this quest grants a key item, so there is no evidence anywhere; the Sanctus Rosary is the Reward and rule 7 rules it out in any case, though it matters in the next quest.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 6: the honest imp is redrawn each game day, so no name can be recorded: it is Rikke (G-7), Rakke (G-10) or Rokke (H-10) on the first map, and the page's three-scenario table resolves it from what they say about each other.

notes: The header names Volker in Castle Zvahl Baileys (S) as the giver, but bullet 1 says the quest opens when you ZONE into Baileys (S) from Keep (S) -- Volker is almost certainly a cutscene actor at that zone line rather than a standing entity. His name is kept in start.npc because an unmatched name simply never draws (a silent loss, not a wrong marker) and the header string is preserved verbatim in start.raw; the real trigger is flagged as a zone entry. Bullet 4 holds three actions and splits into three rungs -- examine to spawn, kill, examine again -- and the third grants the Zvahl passkey, the only observable thing in the entire quest. Bullets 5 and 6 are the same door twice, so they merge: the first examine is a cutscene, the second enters the battlefield, and the marker never moves between them. I read 'Enter the Throne Room (S), and examine the Throne Room door' literally -- the door is a battlefield entrance INSIDE zone Throne Room (S), not the way into it -- because bullet 5 puts the zone entry first and bullet 6 has the door leading onward to the BC. If that reading is wrong the door and the fight belong in Castle Zvahl Keep (S) instead, which is why those three steps are individually medium and the quest with them. The page never says where the Zvahl passkey is spent; presumably on the way to the throne room, but it is not stated, so the passkey is evidence where it is granted and appears in no step's items -- putting it in items would be inventing a requirement. The first BC opponent is described in detail but never named, so only Marquis Amon is recorded as a mob; Zeid is an ally, not a target, and the battle ends if he falls. The last sub-bullet under bullet 7 is a genuine optional action -- a second conversation for Trust Magic: Klara, gated on holding the Bundle of half-inscribed scrolls -- and the closing line pointing at Adieu, Lilisette is a mission signpost, not a step. The Excelsis Ring is the Reward and can never be evidence.
